history.dynasty: Unknown (no documented dynasty; local bijesthali tradition)
history.period: Unknown — visitor and travel sources call it 'ancient'; exact founding date unverified
history.summary: Maa Ambika, revered by the people of Baripada and the whole Mayurbhanj district (and devotees from Jharkhand and West Bengal) as 'The Living Goddess', presides from an ancient marble chaturbhuja (four-armed) idol seated on a lion, holding dambaru, khadga, kharpara and trisula. It is the town's chief Shakti temple (bijesthali) with a moderate-sized complex, painted outer walls, interior mythological paintings, and shrines to Shiva (Ambikeswar Mahadev), Ganesha, Panchamukhi Hanuman, Maa Mangala, Chandika and others. HISTORY FLAG: founding date is unverified — sources disagree; one travel blog dates a 'Maa Ambika Temple' built by the King of Mayurbhanj to 1940 but describes it beside a waterfall near Udala (Devkund, ~50 km from town) near Simlipal, suggesting a different Ambika shrine; the 1940 date is not verified for this Baripada-town temple. Coordinates from geocoder (matched 'Ambika Temple, Meher Colony, Baripada' — consistent with the heart-of-town location).

name: Maa Ambika Temple
town_description: Baripada is the district headquarters town of Mayurbhanj district in northern Odisha, at the foothills of the Simlipal range. A historic Bhanja-dynasty princely capital and temple town, it hosts the Ambika temple in the heart of the town (~1 km from the bus stand).

travel.airport: Bhubaneswar (~270 km) and Kolkata (~240 km) are the nearest airports (distances per tourmyodisha)
travel.road: ~1 km from Baripada bus stand (per tourmyodisha); reachable by local transport within the town

visitor_information.best_time: October–March; Durga Puja and Navratri are the most vibrant seasons
